title: Stage Magic on Your Doorstep: Creative Burntwood Project Unveils Jam-Packed Year Two Season
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: From interactive Shakespeare and pyjama Halloween parties to £5 baby sensory music and festive Dickensian classics, Lichfield Garrick’s Creative Burntwood project unveils an action-packed new season for families and local theatregoers.
bodyHtml:
Bringing the arts directly into the heart of our local communities is where real stage magic begins. Now heading into its second exciting year, the Creative Burntwood project—led by the Lichfield Garrick Theatre in partnership with Burntwood Town Council and Lichfield District Council—is continuing its mission to enrich local culture, enliven neighbourhood venues, and make live performance welcoming and accessible to all.

Supported by Arts Council England’s Place Partnership Fund, the outreach initiative follows an incredible first year featuring social media sensation Jonny Cole, top-tier comedy from Manford’s Comedy Club, and high-flying children's circus shows.

This autumn and winter, the project returns with an even richer programme crafted especially for curious young minds, growing families, and relaxed community outings.

Younger theatregoers can kick off the new school year on 20th September with Magical Honey at Chase Terrace Community Centre—a spellbinding blend of South Asian dance, live music, and cultural storytelling celebrating the triumph of art over adversity (Ages 5+). Creative hands will love MakeBeth at Ashmole Bowls & Social Club on 11th October, where Shakespeare's classic is reinvented through interactive cardboard crafting (Ages 7+).

For Halloween, slip on your cosy sleepwear for The Witch Who Couldn't Sleep at Burntwood Memorial Institute on 25th October—a sensory-friendly, interactive pyjama party blending animation, atmospheric lighting, and call-and-response storytelling where children guide the plot (Ages 3+).

The family programme stretches well into 2027 with non-verbal bunraku puppetry in Secrets of the Selkie Sea (16th January, Ages 6+) and puppet encounters in The Zoo that Comes to You at Burntwood Library (7th April, Ages 5+). Finding budget-friendly sensory adventures for tiny tots can often be tough, but Babies Adventures in Music brings an inspiring, accessible sensory session to Burntwood Memorial Institute on 15th March for just £5 (Ages 0–18 months).

Grown-ups are equally well catered for with the return of Manford’s Comedy Club (26th September), BBC Radio 2 Folk Award winners Kathryn Roberts & Sean Lakeman (7th October), and spine-lingering ghost stories in Tales After Dark at Burntwood Library (18th March).

When the festive season arrives, experience a Dickensian classic staged in the atmospheric setting of St Anne’s Church with A Christmas Carol (4th December, complete with optional mince pies and mulled wine), or join Father Christmas’ reindeer caretaker in A Christmas Story at Ashmole Bowls & Social Club (12th December) for an uplifting journey about communication, empathy, and festive cheer.
detailsHtml:
• Project: Creative Burntwood (Year 2 Outreach Season)

  • Lead Partners: Lichfield Garrick Theatre, Burntwood Town Council & Lichfield District Council (Supported by Arts Council England)

  • Key Venues: Burntwood Memorial Institute, Chase Terrace Community Centre, Burntwood Library, St Anne’s Church & Ashmole Bowls and Social Club

  • Family Highlights: Magical Honey (20 Sep), MakeBeth (11 Oct), The Witch Who Couldn't Sleep (25 Oct), A Christmas Carol (4 Dec), A Christmas Story (12 Dec), Secrets of the Selkie Sea (16 Jan), Babies Adventures in Music (15 Mar), The Zoo that Comes to You (7 Apr)

  • Box Office / Phone: 01543 412121

  • Online Booking & Workshops: creativeburntwood.com

title: Birmingham Royal Ballet Cygnets Take to the Water Ahead of Swan Lake at Birmingham Hippodrome
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: Birmingham Royal Ballet’s cygnets made a splash at Cannon Hill Park’s boating lake to celebrate Sir Peter Wright’s Swan Lake heading to Birmingham Hippodrome and London's Sadler's Wells this autumn.
bodyHtml:
Dancers from Birmingham Royal Ballet made a splash at Cannon Hill Park’s boating lake this week, striking a pose alongside the iconic swan boats to celebrate the upcoming revival of Sir Peter Wright and Galina Samsova’s world-renowned production of Swan Lake.

The company’s first cast of four cygnets — Rachele Pizzillo, Reina Fuchigami, Rosanna Ely, and Sofia Liñares — took time out of intensive rehearsals to visit the historic Birmingham park, posing on the water before taking to the stage at Birmingham Hippodrome from Wednesday 23 September to Saturday 3 October 2026.

The cygnets in Swan Lake perform the iconic Danse des petits cygnes (Dance of the Little Swans) in Act II — one of the most recognisable and demanding pieces of classical choreography in ballet. The four dancers must cross arms in unbroken formation and move in precise, flawless unison, capturing young cygnets huddling together.

Set to Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky’s legendary score performed live by the Royal Ballet Sinfonia, the ballet tells the timeless story of Prince Siegfried and Odette, a princess cursed by the sorcerer Baron von Rothbart to live as a swan by day and a woman by night.

Birmingham & London Ages 5+ Live Orchestra

Following its ten-day run at Birmingham Hippodrome, the production will transfer to London’s Sadler’s Wells Theatre from Wednesday 28 to Saturday 31 October 2026.

Families looking to get a closer look at the world of classical ballet can also catch Birmingham Royal Ballet in the city centre this weekend as part of Birmingham Weekender in the Bullring on Saturday 29 August, featuring free Swan Lake children's dance workshops.

Swan Lake Performance & Booking Details

  • Birmingham Hippodrome: Wednesday 23 September – Saturday 3 October 2026
  • Sadler’s Wells, London: Wednesday 28 October – Saturday 31 October 2026
  • Music: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, played live by the Royal Ballet Sinfonia
  • Choreography & Production: Sir Peter Wright and Galina Samsova
  • Family & Sensory Note: Features atmospheric stage lighting and dramatic live orchestral climaxes. Birmingham Hippodrome offers accessible seating and dedicated quiet spaces for families.
  • Tickets & Information: Book online via brb.org.uk

title: London Theatre Week Is Back: It’s Like Christmas Come Early for Theatre Fans!
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: London Theatre Week has officially returned with exclusive West End ticket offers from just £15, £25, and £35! Discover incredible savings across more than 80 major productions, including family favourites like The Lion King, Oliver!, and Wicked.
bodyHtml:
If your household loves the buzz of live theatre as much as ours does, consider this the ultimate treat: Special Promotion — London Theatre Week has arrived, and it truly feels like Christmas come early!

The West End’s biggest ticket promotion of the season is officially live, opening up access to more than 80 world-class shows with exclusive, set promotional pricing from just £15, £25, and £35. Whether you’re looking to introduce your little ones to their very first big musical, secure brilliant seats for an autumn weekend getaway, or lock in half-term and festive treats well before the rush, this is the single best time of the year to grab incredible bargains.

Our Personal Family Favourites Included

What makes this year’s London Theatre Week lineup especially magical is that some of our absolute all-time family favourites are included in the exclusive pricing tiers:

  • The Lion King (Lyceum Theatre): Pure theatrical magic from the very first opening call of the Circle of Life. Julie Taymor’s breathtaking puppetry and visual grandeur make it an unforgettable sensory spectacle for kids of all ages.

  • Oliver! (Gielgud Theatre): Lionel Bart’s classic masterpiece is back in London, packed with timeless tunes, irresistible energy, and rich storytelling that captivates every generation.

  • Wicked (Apollo Victoria Theatre): The gravity-defying emerald phenomenon remains one of the most spellbinding, empowering, and visually thrilling experiences on the London stage.

Unbeatable Value Across 80+ West End Shows

Beyond our top picks, the promotional roster covers dozens of acclaimed musicals, blockbuster family plays, and immersive experiences—including Matilda The Musical, Les Misérables, The Phantom of the Opera, Back to the Future: The Musical, Mamma Mia!, and The Play That Goes Wrong.

Taking children to West End shows can sometimes feel like a daunting investment, particularly when navigating travel and sensory requirements. Campaigns like London Theatre Week take the pressure off by unlocking premium tiers and circle seats at a fraction of standard peak pricing. Ticket allocations at these fixed price bands are limited and sell fast, so be sure to check dates and book early!
detailsHtml:
• Promotion Name: London Theatre Week

  • Ticket Price Tiers: Exclusive fixed-price bands from £15, £25, and £35 across participating performances.

  • Featured Highlights: Over 80+ productions including The Lion King, Oliver!, Wicked, Matilda, Les Misérables, and Back to the Future.

  • Booking Window: Limited-time seasonal campaign (availability on a first-come, first-served basis).

  • Official Booking Link: Explore all London Theatre Week deals on TodayTix →

  • BTMC Parent Tip: When booking, check the venue's access page or visual story in advance to pick aisle seats or lower-tier circle rows that give younger or neurodivergent children clear views and easy exit paths.

  • Plan your journey well: We like to map out tubes in advance and where possible travel to quieter stations like Marylebone, which provides a direct line into Theatreland via the the Bakerloo line disembarking in 4 stops at Picadilly Circus.

title: A New Stage Begins: Behind The Magic Curtain Officially Relaunches
author: Katy Rose Meaney
summary: We are proud to unveil the brand-new Behind The Magic Curtain — rebuilt from the ground up to bring UK families detailed neurodivergent theatre guides, sensory ratings, and West End touring insights.
bodyHtml:
When my son turned to me in tears after his very first show in 2019 and whispered, "Mummy, please go behind the magic curtain and ask them to come back and see me," a spark was ignited. Over the years, as our family learned to navigate ADHD, sensory overstimulation, and an enduring passion for live performance, that spark grew into Behind The Magic Curtain.

Today, we are thrilled to raise the curtain on our completely relaunched website. We have redesigned every part of the platform to remove the guesswork, stress, and anxiety from planning family theatre visits and immersive days out.

Here is what you will find across the new platform:

  • Sensory Strategies — In-depth parent insights covering sudden sound spikes, lighting effects, queue management, and quiet break spaces for all featured productions.

  • What's On & UK Tours — Up-to-date tracking of West End transfers, regional Midlands venues, and accessible relaxed performances.

  • Venue Accessibility Directory — Step-free access audits, hearing loops, and sensory breakout spaces across regional theatres.

Live theatre has the power to inspire every child. Our mission is to ensure every family feels confident walking through the foyer doors, finding their seats, and experiencing the wonder together.

Take a look around the new site, test out the interactive guides, and join our community newsletter below to stay updated on all upcoming productions and relaxed performances.

Katy x
detailsHtml:
• Website: behindthemagiccurtain.co.uk

  • Core Features: Sensory Reviews, What's On Guide and Theatre tips

  • Focus Areas: Family Theatre, ADHD Strategies & Relaxed Performances

  • Editorial Enquiries: Hello@behindthemagiccurtain.co.uk
